2: For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. Hear this, all you peoples; give ear, all you inhabitants of the world,
3: both low and high, rich and poor together.
4: My mouth will speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart will be understanding.
5: I will incline my ear to a proverb; I will ⌞propound⌟ my riddle on a lyre.
6: Why should I fear in ⌞times of calamity⌟, when iniquity surrounds me at my heels,
7: those who trust their wealth and boast about the abundance of their riches?
8: Surely a man cannot redeem a brother. He cannot give to God his ransom
9: (since the redemption price for their life is costly and it always fails),
10: so that he may stay alive forever and not see the pit.
11: For he sees that the wise die, together with the fool and brute they perish, and leave their wealth to the next generation.
12: Within them they think their houses are forever, their dwelling places from generation to generation. They ⌞name⌟ their lands by their own names.
13: But man cannot continue in his pomp. He is like the beasts that perish.
14: This is the journey of those who have foolish confidence, and those after them who accept their sayings. Selah
15: Like sheep they are destined to Sheol; death will shepherd them. But the upright will rule over them in the morning, and their forms will be for Sheol to consume, far from his lofty abode.
16: Surely God will ransom my life from the ⌞power⌟ of Sheol, because he will receive me. Selah
17: Do not fear when a man becomes rich, when the wealth of his house increases,
18: because when he dies he will not take away any of it. His wealth will not follow down after him.
19: Though he congratulated his soul while he was living —and people will praise you when you do well for yourself—
20: it will go to the generation of his fathers. Never will they see light.
21: Humankind in its pomp, but does not understand, is like the beasts that perish.
